kind.description: What happened. Only scoring plays ('score') for now.

team.description: com.professorbutts.sports.team record of the side the points count for (for an own goal, the team that benefits).

text.description: The play as the source describes it.

clock.description: Game clock or match minute as shown, e.g. '4:12' or "67'".

period.description: Period of the play, as on the game record, e.g. {number: 5, label: 'OT'}, {number: 7, label: 'Top 7th'}.

points.description: Points this play added, including a kick or conversion the source reports with it (7 for a touchdown plus kick).

source.description: Where the data came from, e.g. 'espn'.

status.description: Leave out for a play that stands. 'overturned': reversed by the officials. 'removed': the source dropped or replaced it for another or unknown reason (see replacedBy). Readers treat any value, including ones they don't know, as a play that doesn't count.

sequence.description: Sort order among this game's plays. Gaps are fine; not renumbered when a play is removed.

scoreType.description: Kind of score, e.g. 'touchdown', 'goal', 'home-run'. 'penalty-goal' covers soccer penalties and rugby penalty kicks.

occurredAt.description: Wall-clock time of the play, when the source gives it.

replacedBy.description: The play record that replaces this one, when the source re-entered the play under a new ID.

externalIds.description: The play's ID at the source, e.g. {scheme: 'espn', value: '401772936101'}.

scoringSide.description: Which side the points count for. Set it even when there's no team record.

main.description: Record key is '<game rkey>-<source play id>', e.g. 'nfl-401772936-401772936101', so a game's plays sit together in key order. Created once per source play and updated only to correct it or set status. A play the source drops keeps its record with a status, so posts that link to it keep resolving.

description: One scoring play in a game, as its own record linked to the game. Game records are updated in place; plays are kept, so together they are the game's scoring history (for scoring-play cards or game-thread replies). Basketball baskets are not written as plays.
